2026-10-02 assessment of the upstream fix (reframe4s bd-01M3WRE7BEJFR3G67BBEBH2NGE, closed). PointwiseInversion lands at 5f7152aada60335935843ddc968162f615337415. Its parent is the ScalaFIM pin 9a450835 (+3 files, +497 lines), and it is on origin/main via a4a8c0c, so it is pinnable by SHA.
Code review: matches the scoped request. Per-query result carries best iterate, residual, iterations and status (Converged / MaxIterations / Diverged / LeftSupport / Failure). The affine is removed analytically, iteration starts from identity, and there is no lattice, warm start or retry. Not a SpatialMap or SmoothIso. Outside support or source-preserving extension is LeftSupport, never filled. Docs disclaim invertibility, uniqueness and consumer qualification. No defects found.
Provider tests re-run independently: reframe4s-fieldJVM 22/22 and fieldJS 22/22.
Real-data assessment (uncommitted RealPointwiseInverseSuite, ScalaFIM built against the reframe4s worktree via -Dscalafim.reframe4s.build; library defaults: 100 iterations, tolerance 1e-8 mm, divergence 4), all 64,984 fsLR vertices vs the all-vertex SimpleITK oracle:
- status Converged 32492/32492 per hemisphere; max iterations 30 (L) / 20 (R); max residual 1.0e-8 mm
- placement vs oracle max 1.50e-8 / 1.53e-8 mm, p99 1.07e-8 / 1.06e-8 mm
- nearest-voxel disagreements 0 on both the 2009c res-01 (1 mm) and res-02 (2 mm) grids, all vertices and cortex. The consumer fixtures are on the res-02 grid, so mapped values and support there equal the oracle placement's.
- cost: 2.6 s (L) + 1.9 s (R) single-threaded JVM, versus 135-224 s and 2.3 GB for the lattice; RSS 1.9 GB, dominated by loading the point map.
Remaining before admission (ScalaFIM-owned): pin bump to 5f7152aa (build.sbt is currently reserved by umvpa-finish-20261001 until 2026-10-02T12:53Z); a bridge use backed by PointwiseInversion with per-vertex status/residual/iteration receipts and the BridgeExactness evidence generalization; retire the lattice path; freeze value-level budgets and re-run FslrBridgeDisagreement through the production bridge; real Scala.js cost; fresh-context review; gates on both platforms.
